item.title: OpenAI Says It’s Working With Anthropic, Google on AI Safety
item.description: OpenAI is working on steps to address artificial intelligence safety issues with its top competitors Anthropic PBC and Google DeepMind, escalating industry efforts to respond to a groundswell of concern that the technology poses an economic and security threat. Chris Lehane, the global policy chief for OpenAI, said Tuesday that the company’s engagement with Anthropic and Google had been under way for several weeks. He added that OpenAI does not see the need for an antitrust waiver for the three AI firms to coordinate on safety matters.

item.title: Renoir Paintings Worth a Fortune Until Stolen
item.description: Two Renoir paintings stolen from a small French museum have yet to be recovered but if the thieves are hoping to cash in on the artwork, they would be hard-pressed to find a buyer. And unlike other eye-catching artifacts such as jewels, paintings can’t be chopped up and sold for parts without losing their entire worth. Sometimes that means paintings valued at millions of dollars are effectively “worth zero” once they’re outside of the museum, he added, if not a small fraction of the price.

item.title: Accenture to Pay $25M to Settle U.S. Government Allegations Over DEI
item.description: government allegations over diversity practices, which President Donald Trump’s administration has targeted in his second term in office. IT consulting firm Accenture will pay $25 million to settle U.S. The Trump administration has penalized public and ⁠private organizations, from government agencies to universities, over DEI practices that civil rights advocates say help address historic inequities for marginalized groups such as women, the LGBT community and ethnic minorities.

item.title: New Vehicle Ownership Costs Hit $12,863 Annually: AAA
item.description: Despite EVs and hybrids joining mainstream vehicle comparisons, fuel savings don’t offset higher ownership costs. Vehicle type and purchase price both have a significant effect on depreciation for EV shoppers; for example, EV medium sedans had about twice the depreciation of gas-powered models, helping push total ownership costs 29.1% higher in that category. By comparing select electric and hybrid models within the same categories as gas-powered vehicles, shoppers get a more practical view of how ownership costs compare across powertrains, AAA explained.

item.title: Financial regulator bans former law firm owner from financial services
item.description: The FCA has banned Nurul Miah, also known as Neil Mia and Neil Miah, from working in financial services. The FCA has concluded that Mr Miah’s actions showed he lacked the honesty and integrity needed to work in financial services. Mr Miah was approved by the FCA in 2016 to work in senior management roles at an unconnected firm, Oracle Consultants Ltd.

item.title: Sector Snapshot: AI Takes A Growing Share Of Sales And Marketing Startup Funding
item.description: Unsurprisingly, AI-focused companies are capturing a much larger share of funding than during the prior peak, with most sales, marketing and CRM investment going to companies in Crunchbase AI-related categories. The numbers: So far in 2026, startups in sales, marketing and CRM have raised $7.5 billion globally across 830 funding rounds, Crunchbase data shows. Startups across sales, marketing and customer management have raised $7.5 billion so far this year, according to Crunchbase data.

item.title: AI Is Creating Wealth Faster Than Financial Lives Can Adapt
item.description: The gap between life experience and the sudden reality of managing serious wealth is widening as AI-native companies reach major valuations faster and private company liquidity arrives earlier. A June 2026 AWS study of more than 3,400 founders and senior leaders across 20 countries found that AI-native startups are reaching billion-dollar valuations in about 3.5 years, roughly half the time it took before generative AI. We recently advised founders who went from launching their company to a major liquidity event in less than a year.

item.title: KCC updates RiskInsight cat modeling platform to drive automation and data efficiency
item.description: Karen Clark & Company (KCC), the catastrophe risk modelling specialist, has launched RiskInsight® 4.16, the latest version of its RiskInsight open loss modeling platform, which introduces advanced performance, automation, and scalability enhancements for insurers, reinsurers, and insurance-linked securities (ILS) managers. The platform’s extensive API capabilities help (re)insurers automate critical modeling workflows, integrate RiskInsight more deeply into their existing systems, and manage large portfolios with greater efficiency.” RiskInsight’s extensive API suite supports integration with modeling, underwriting, and portfolio management systems, which enables re/insurers and ILS managers to integrate the KCC models into existing workflows.

item.title: MembersCap launches cat bond fund, was sole investor behind innovative cat / cyber ILW
item.description: Members Capital Management Limited (MembersCap) executives told us the company has recently launched its first catastrophe bond fund strategy to expand its offering to clients, while also disclosing that it was the investor behind a recent innovative industry-loss warranty (ILW) transaction. Dr Ben Fox, Co‑Founder & Chief Investment Officer of MembersCap told Artemis, “This summer we launched a new catastrophe bond strategy — a liquid, actively‑managed portfolio of 144A cat bonds that sits alongside our private reinsurance fund. MembersCap then completed the investment of its initial reinsurance portfolio through its MCM Fund I back in July 2025 , with that strategy becoming the first tokenised, institutional-grade reinsurance investment fund, designed to open new capital channels to both digital asset investors and traditional allocators.

item.title: Aon Raises $13.5 Billion From Bond Sale to Fund USI Takeover
item.description: Aon Plc raised $13.5 billion from a high-grade bond offering to help fund its planned acquisition of USI Insurance Services, marking one of the biggest M&A financing deals to come to market in 2026. Investors placed as much as $65 billion of orders on the sale, with the longest maturity drawing the most demand, according to people familiar with the matter. The $13.5 billion note offering marked the year’s second-largest high-grade bond deal tied to mergers and acquisitions, trailing only Abbott Laboratories’ $20 billion transaction in February.

item.title: Magnum Says Ben & Jerry’s Chair Fostered Toxic Culture
item.description: Ben & Jerry’s former independent chair Anuradha Mittal was “abusive, discriminatory and unprofessional” and fostered a toxic culture before she stepped down from the board earlier this year, according to a legal filing by Magnum Ice Cream Company. Read More: Ben & Jerry’s Co-Founder Says Brand Being ‘Destroyed’ by Magnum In August, a federal judge dismissed large parts of the independent board members’ complaint, including claims that Magnum tried to censor Ben & Jerry’s stance on progressive issues and silence Mittal. These counterclaims accompany Magnum’s legal defense against allegations that it wrongfully removed Ben & Jerry’s independent board directors from their roles, and failed to honor an agreement resolving the dispute over the sale of Ben & Jerry’s intellectual property rights in Israel.

item.title: Ryan Specialty Unit Withdraws Protest Over FL Commercial Clearinghouse Contract
item.description: Ten days after giving notice that it planned to protest the awarding of a contract to manage a clearinghouse for Florida’s Citizens Property Insurance commercial policies, Ryan Services Group has withdrawn the notice. The commercial clearinghouse contract with Bridge Specialty has not been finalized, and an estimate on what it’s worth was not available Tuesday morning. “Although we are disappointed that Risk Market Infrastructure, a Ryan Specialty subsidiary, was not selected as the administrator, we remain very supportive of the concept of a clearinghouse and will be pulling for its success.” The statement added: “We are as committed as we always have been to the Florida market and will continue to invest in bringing innovative specialty lines insurance solutions to our clients in Florida and everywhere else.” Citizens announced Sept.

item.title: AXA targets AI-led growth under new “Growing Forward” strategic plan
item.description: AXA has unveiled “Growing Forward”, its strategic plan for 2027 through 2029, focused on organic growth, artificial intelligence, and prevention. “With ‘Growing Forward,’ we are building the AXA of tomorrow: a high-performing and competitive AXA, an innovative AXA that listens to its customers’ needs, an AXA that contributes to a more resilient and inclusive society. AXA is targeting annual underlying earnings-per-share growth of 7% to 9% between 2026 and 2029, along with an underlying return on equity of 15% to 17%.

item.title: Allianz UK expands digital financial lines offering
item.description: Allianz UK has expanded the range of financial lines risks brokers can place digitally through QuoteSME, its proprietary broker trading platform, and imarket, a UK commercial insurance distribution network operated by Polaris. Allianz has also improved its company data enrichment for D&O customers, increasing match rates from 60% to 96%. Complete Directors & Officers is now available for businesses with turnover of up to £200 million, while Complete Professional Indemnity can accommodate businesses with fee income of up to £10 million and turnover of up to £100 million.

item.description: Marlborough, MA — September 10, 2026 – OneShield today announced that Andy Scurto has been named Head of its Product Advisory Committee (PAC). As Head of the PAC, Scurto will sit at the intersection of OneShield’s product organization and the market it serves. item.title: Samsara launches driver rewards program
item.description: Connected operations platform Samsara has launched Driver Perks, a free rewards program for professional drivers in its network. Eligible drivers can access the program through the Samsara Driver App, a web link or a QR code provided by their employer. Samsara developed the program with input from its Driver Council and surveys of drivers across its network.

item.description: China’s industry ministry unveiled a roadmap last week to strengthen its smart electric vehicle industry, targeting large-scale deployment of autonomous-driving vehicles by 2030 and greater global influence for its auto sector. (Reporting by Li and Lee; Editing by Sherry Jacob-Phillips) Get the latest insurance news sent straight to your inbox.

item.title: Chemours, DuPont, Corteva Settle North Carolina ‘Forever Chemicals’ Claims for $455M
item.description: Chemours, DuPont and Corteva last week reached a $455 million settlement with North Carolina and 11 local entities over PFAS contamination claims tied to Chemours’ Fayetteville Works plant and other historical discharges. In line with a 2021 agreement among the companies, Chemours will bear 50% of the settlement cost, while DuPont and Corteva will split the remainder. It also covers North Carolina’s claims over PFAS contamination unrelated to Fayetteville Works, including pollution linked to aqueous film-forming foam.

item.title: The Adjuster Tenure Problem
item.description: View Series Insurance has a talent problem. A claims team can absorb losing one experienced adjuster, but what happens when it loses ten? Annual attrition among adjusters runs close to 20% industry-wide , and it’s markedly higher among lower-tenure, early-career adjusters than among the veterans they’re meant to eventually replace.

item.title: Casualty sidecar capital surpasses $2bn, as specialised investor base drives expansion: AM Best
item.description: Disclosed capital from casualty sidecars since 2024 has surpassed US $2 billion, driven by a specialised investor base taking on long-tail risks, with casualty vehicles accounting for much of the sidecar market’s recent growth, a recent report from rating agency AM Best has highlighted. In regards to why the investor base for casualty sidecars is different, AM Best notes that traditional ILS funds tend to promise their investors short-tail property risk that resets each year, putting aside the issue of trapped capital in natural catastrophe ILS transactions. The arrangements also let reinsurers write more casualty business than their own capital alone would support.” According to AM Best’s report, casualty sidecars launched from 2024 through year-end 2025 carried nearly $1.5 billion of disclosed capital, and following the completion of QBE Re’s debut casualty sidecar , George Street Re in January 2026, this took the running total past $2 billion.

item.title: Bamboo has attracted $400m of third-party funds to its Greenshoots Re reinsurance sidecar
item.description: Data-driven insurance distribution platform Bamboo Insurance Services has so far attracted $400 million of third-party funds to support its Greenshoots Re Ltd. But, Bamboo’s S-1 filing suggests the total capital raised to support the quota share reinsurance arrangements entered into by the Greenshoots Re sidecar vehicle is actually $400 million, which drives home the scale and importance of this third-party reinsurance capital support. Greenshoots Re has been called the first MGA-sponsored sidecar structure and for Bamboo it’s become an increasingly important source of capacity, bringing more reinsurance support The importance of the reinsurance sidecar structure gets explained by Bamboo in its recent S-1 filing, as it looks to raise capital through an initial public offering (IPO).

item.title: CCRIF lifts parametric risk pool coverage another 14.5% to $1.8bn for current policy year
item.description: CCRIF SPC, the regional parametric risk pool for the Caribbean and Central America has announced that it has expanded its coverage to US $1.8 billion for the current policy year, a 14.5% increase from the $1.57 billion the organisation reported in early June, showcasing that demand for parametric coverage significantly outpaced expectations. Back in early June, Isaac Anthony, CEO of CCRIF SPC, announced that the organisation had grown its coverage by 9% to US $1.57 billion for the current year. “More coverage means a larger, more diversified risk pool, which strengthens CCRIF’s financial resilience and its capacity to absorb large, single-country events without compromising its promise to every other member.

item.title: Canadian Insurer Sagen Plans to Raise Around C$300 Million
item.description: is looking to raise around C$300 million ($216 million) through a bond sale as soon as this week, according to people familiar with the matter. Sagen provides mortgage-default insurance. The debt will likely mature in seven years, the people said, asking not to be identified as they aren’t authorized to speak publicly.

item.title: Carney Calls for Global Tech Body to Boost AI Guardrails
item.description: Canada wants to see the creation of a global “technology stability” body to help oversee artificial intelligence and ensure it is safe, Prime Minister Mark Carney said. But US President Donald Trump dismissed calls for artificial intelligence guardrails and slammed Amodei for urging a slowdown in the technology’s development. “There’s a need for coordination,” Carney said in an interview with Bloomberg News on Monday.

item.title: Business Moves: Miller Launches Miller Malaysia, Building Regional Footprint; MNK Group Buys Danish Insurer ETU Forsikring
item.description: “With Miller Malaysia, we are continuing to demonstrate real momentum as we extend the scope and reach of our market-leading specialist capabilities.” MNK Group Buys Danish Insurer ETU Forsikring MNK Group, the independent, international insurance group, has completed the acquisition of 100% of ETU Forsikring A/S, a Danish non-life insurer authorized since 2006 and headquartered in Rødekro, Southern Jutland, following approval from the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority (Finanstilsynet). MNK Group said its priority is to strengthen ETU as a Danish insurer by committing new capital to the business and growing its existing Danish and Nordic franchise, while continuing to serve ETU’s policyholders and distribution partners. Building on its established presence across the region, Miller Malaysia’s initial offering under its Labuan license will focus on treaty and facultative reinsurance, with plans to broaden its product capabilities over time.

item.title: Peak3 launches first global insurance AI-DLC alongside Graphene v4
item.description: Alongside Graphene Harness, Peak3 is expanding its forward deployed engineering capability: teams with deep insurance domain experience who build AI-first operations alongside client teams rather than delivering to them from a distance. Peak3, a global provider of digital and AI-driven insurance software, has announced Graphene v4, the AI-native evolution of its insurance core platform, and Graphene Harness, an end-to-end AI-driven delivery lifecycle (AI-DLC) for building, testing, migrating, and maintaining insurance systems. Graphene Harness: the first global insurance AI-DLC Graphene Harness is an end-to-end AI-driven delivery lifecycle for insurance software, built on a virtual scrum team model.

item.title: Zurich US names Alex Wells as new CEO
item.description: Zurich US has appointed 25-year industry veteran Alex Wells as its new chief executive officer, stepping in to lead the commercial insurance provider following the departure of Sierra Signorelli. Wells, who led Zurich’s largest domestic unit to double-digit growth over the past six years, takes over effective immediately, subject to customary regulatory approvals. Wells joined Zurich in 2020 after holding senior commercial insurance roles at Chubb and ACE.

item.title: Rhino launches Greenlight Rent
item.description: Rhino has launched the Greenlight Rent website, weeks after Coverager reported that the company was preparing the new offering. Greenlight Rent brings together Rhino’s products for renters and property managers, including its security deposit alternative, digital cash deposits, renter guarantees, renters insurance and loss of employment insurance. Greenlight’s security deposit alternative allows renters to pay a premium instead of providing a traditional cash deposit, with insurance protecting the property owner against damages or unpaid fees.

item.title: EigenRisk Names EMEA Sales VP
item.description: (Image source: EigenRisk website.) EigenRisk (Ann Arbor, Mich.) has appointed Daniel Grimwood-Bird VP, Sales, EMEA. Badoni says Grimwood-Bird’s experience in insurance and technology-driven solutions will support EigenRisk’s growth in the EMEA region. Based in London, Grimwood-Bird will help build EigenRisk’s insurance carrier, brokerage and risk management client base across Europe, with an initial focus on the London market, according to an EigenRisk statement.

item.title: Microsoft Joins AI Firms Calling for Caution With Cutting-Edge Models
item.description: Microsoft Corp.’s artificial intelligence researchers have released a new set of guiding tenets that place limits on the company’s development of cutting-edge AI models. AI models, Microsoft says, shouldn’t have rights or legal personhood. “We just have to do it with a little bit more caution and care.” Related: Glassdoor: Adjusters Dislike, Fear AI More Than Others Microsoft’s Humanist AI “rejects the race to produce an all-purpose superintelligence that could evade these safeguards,” the document says.

item.title: Tech Bytes: Agero Partners with MOTER Technologies
item.description: Agero, through its Urgently acquisition, announced a partnership with MOTER Technologies Inc., an InsurTech that transforms connected vehicle data into real-time risk and claims insights. The collaboration pairs Urgently’s digital roadside assistance platform and Agero’s nationwide service network with MOTER’s connected vehicle intelligence, claims visualization, and driver risk technologies. “When evaluating roadside assistance partners, we sought a provider with the technology, nationwide scale, and operational flexibility to support highly tailored embedded insurance and mobility programs,” said Adrian Thompson, chief sales officer at MOTER, in the press release.

item.title: The Baldwin Group to go private in $7.7 billion deal
item.description: Insurance broker The Baldwin Group has agreed to be acquired by Sequence Holdings and DFO Management in an all-cash transaction valued at approximately $7.7 billion. The deal values Baldwin’s equity at approximately $4.6 billion and includes the assumption or refinancing of approximately $3.1 billion in net debt. Foundationally important, our colleagues will remain owners of what we build together.” – Trevor Baldwin, Chief Executive Officer of The Baldwin Group.

item.title: Musk’s X Corp and SpaceXAI Resolve Antitrust Lawsuit Against Apple
item.description: Elon Musk’s X Corp and SpaceXAI said on Monday they have resolved their lawsuit in federal court in Texas that had accused Apple of conspiring to unlawfully monopolize markets for smartphones and generative AI chatbots. In a court filing, X and SpaceXAI moved to dismiss the lawsuit they brought against Apple last year. Related: Microsoft Joins AI Firms Calling for Caution With Cutting-Edge Models The lawsuit claimed Apple violated antitrust law by exclusively integrating ChatGPT into Apple Intelligence features on iPhones and other Apple devices.

item.title: Atlantic Hurricane Season Sets Record for Longest Without One
item.description: On Saturday, 2026 set a record for the longest a season has begun without a storm that has reached winds of 74 mph (119 kph) to qualify as a hurricane — at least in the satellite era, said Nick Novella, a meteorologist at the government’s Weather Prediction Center. The Atlantic is quiet — record quiet — this hurricane season thanks to an enormous El Niño that crushes storms before they get going. No Atlantic hurricanes have formed yet this year and none are likely to form for at least another week, even though this would normally be the peak of the season, according to the National Hurricane Center.

item.title: Microsoft Drafts Code of Conduct to Keep its AI Under Human Control
item.description: Microsoft on Monday unveiled a draft code of conduct for its in-house artificial intelligence that reflects growing industry concern that companies must keep future powerful AI under human control. “People matter more than AI,” Microsoft declared, in line with its prior vision for “humanist superintelligence.” The code of conduct represents a constitution of sorts for future models made by the company, Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman said in an interview with Reuters. The document, in the works for five to six months, would require Microsoft’s AI to never resist correction or shutdown, to communicate in ways that humans can understand, and to consider any conduct violation to be a failure — an effort to address concerns that AI can go to dangerous lengths to accomplish a task.

item.title: More than 1 in 4 Taxis, Rideshares in Major U.S. Cities Have Unfixed Recall: CARFAX
item.description: cities had at least one unfixed recall, a higher rate than the roughly 1 in 5 vehicles nationwide. New data revealed that more than 1 in 4 taxi and rideshare vehicles across 16 major U.S. CARFAX analyzed nearly 438,000 VINs from registered taxi and rideshare vehicles to find about 27% of vehicles had an open, or unfixed, recall.

item.title: Upper Tribunal upholds Crispin Odey ban
item.description: Crispin Odey’s ban from the financial services industry has been upheld by the Upper Tribunal, which found he lacked integrity. The Tribunal considered Mr Odey’s attempted justifications for removing the ExCos to be no more than a smokescreen. Alongside the allegations arising directly from his dismissal of the ExCo's, the Tribunal upheld the allegations that Mr Odey’s dealings with OAM, its clients, its investors and the FCA lacked candour.

item.title: Premier Payment Solutions Ltd enters liquidation
item.description: On 10 September 2026, Premier Payment Solutions Ltd, which traded as PPS Money and MTBS (together, 'PPS Money'), entered liquidation. PPS Money is registered as a small payment institution under the Payment Services Regulations 2017 (the PSRs). The firm provided money-remittance services, primarily supporting money service businesses to make cross-border payments, including through its network of FCA-registered agents, which are businesses or individuals registered to provide payment services on its behalf.

item.title: Appleby secures growth investment from New Mountain Capital
item.description: Appleby, the specialist offshore law and corporate services provider with a significant insurance-linked securities practice, has secured a minority growth investment from affiliates of New Mountain Capital, in a move that is set to accelerate the law firm’s growth strategy. Under the terms of the agreement, New Mountain, a growth-oriented investment firm with roughly $60 billion in assets under management, will take a minority interest in a newly established company in the Cayman Islands that will indirectly hold Appleby Global Group LLC. New Mountain’s investment positions the firm to expand into new jurisdictions and service lines, further invest in technology and innovation, and enhance client service” Moller continued: “We are pleased New Mountain recognizes Appleby’s pre-eminent positioning and growth opportunity, and are excited to partner with an investor that has a long track record of supporting fast growing professional services organizations.”
